reason: B opens with the Zong killings rendered scene by scene, with dates, counts and a courtroom aftermath, so the reader is carried by narrative pressure and then handed the legal and economic analysis as consequence rather than as thesis. A stays at the level of general assertion and keeps re-explaining the same idea - that law and profit organised the violence - across the Brookes, Codrington, Barbados code, Stono and the closing synthesis, so each new section restates the previous one in fresh vocabulary. B also moves geographically (Barbados, Jamaica, Brazil, Saint-Domingue, Haiti, Louisiana) with a real sense of escalation toward Dessalines, while A ends roughly where it began.
